mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10Y-2Y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, exceeding a 0.5% month-over-month decline, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input constraints and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of months following a triggered INDPRO decline signal.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, especially if the 3-month change exceeds 0.3 percentage points, signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence rises by > 2 points in the University of Michigan survey during the signal period, contradicting the negative labor market signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that will slow economic growth and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the higher cost of borrowing weighs on investment and consumption.
failure_condition: Real GDP growth accelerates by > 1% YoY during the signal period, indicating that the economy is resistant to the higher interest rates.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts decline by more than 10% year-over-year, it signals a weakening housing market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The NAHB Housing Market Index rises by > 5 points during the signal period, indicating that homebuilder sentiment is improving despite the drop in housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth slows by more than 100,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth slows by > 100k jobs/mo for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims decline by > 10% during the signal period, contradicting the negative signal from slowing payroll growth.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (PCE) growth accelerates by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals a strengthening consumer sector that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index declines by > 5 points during the signal period, indicating that the positive consumption signal may be short-lived.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate exceeds 3% year-over-year, it signals rising inflationary pressures that will erode consumer purchasing power and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the Fed is forced to raise interest rates.
failure_condition: The 10-year breakeven inflation rate (from TIPS) declines by > 0.5% during the signal period, indicating that the market expects the inflation spike to be transitory.
